anomalies.title: The Missing Year
anomalies.body: Between 9 Jan 2014 and 12 Jan 2015 not a single track was played. The account had existed for six months and logged 208 plays. Then it stopped, completely, for longer than it had ever been used.
anomalies.ask: What fills a year that leaves no trace?

anomalies.title: The Skip Cliff
anomalies.body: In 2015, 79% of tracks were skipped — restless, nothing landing. In 2016 that fell to 3.6%. From 2017 to 2021 the skip rate is effectively zero: 11 skips across 103,000 plays. Something stopped searching and started staying.
anomalies.ask: Was it the music that changed, or the person?

anomalies.title: The Conversion
anomalies.body: The Beatles appear in 2016 and never leave. They are the #1 artist in eight of the nine following years. No other artist in the record survives more than three years at the top.
anomalies.ask: Which of your habits started as a phase?

anomalies.title: The Long Night
anomalies.body: Listening between midnight and 5 AM peaks in 2021 at 7,527 plays — more than double 2019. Across the whole record the busiest hour of the day is 23:00, and 8 AM to noon is nearly silent. This is a life lived on the other side of the clock.
anomalies.ask: Who were you talking to at 3 AM?

anomalies.title: Otra Vida
anomalies.body: Spanish-language artists sit at 50–150 plays a year for seven years. In 2022 they hit 993 — Joaquín Sabina alone accounts for 576. The next year it collapses back to 259 and never recovers.
anomalies.ask: What arrived in 2022 and left again?

anomalies.title: The Drift
anomalies.body: After five years of near-zero skipping, 2023 jumps to 23.5% and stays there. The top artists barely change — The Beatles, The Killers, John Mayer. Same records, less patience.
anomalies.ask: Is this boredom, or is this grief?
